**Lemma 4.1 (smoothly generated subgroup).** Let \(\mathcal C\) be a family of smooth maps into a finite-dimensional Lie group \(G\), each defined on a connected open subset of some \(\mathbb R^m\) and taking the value \(e\). The subgroup \(H\) generated by all their values has a connected second-countable Lie-group structure for which its inclusion in \(G\) is an injective immersion. Every finite product of the generating maps, with their parameters varying independently, is smooth as a map into this Lie group. The subgroup topology may be finer than its subspace topology.

**Lemma 5.1 (finite lasso factorization).** Every finitely piecewise \(C^1\) nullhomotopic based loop is a product of finitely many small lassos and their inverses, up to inserting or deleting a path followed by its reverse. The lasso loops may be chosen finitely piecewise \(C^1\). Each lasso's holonomy is a value of a smooth curve of holonomies of nullhomotopic loops starting at the identity.
**Lemma 5.2 (countable fundamental group).** The fundamental group of a connected second-countable manifold is countable.

**Theorem 6.1 (holonomy is an immersed Lie subgroup).** \(\operatorname{Hol}_p^0\) is a connected immersed Lie subgroup of \(G\). It is a normal subgroup of \(\operatorname{Hol}_p\), which is itself an immersed Lie subgroup with identity component \(\operatorname{Hol}_p^0\). The quotient \(\operatorname{Hol}_p/\operatorname{Hol}_p^0\) is countable.

**Proposition 10.1 (intrinsic torsion).** The torsion tensors of two connections preserving the same \(H\)-reduction differ by \(\delta A\), where their difference is the tensor \(A\in T^*M\otimes\mathfrak h_M\). Consequently their common class in the associated quotient bundle with fibre \(\operatorname{coker}\delta\) is intrinsic to the reduction. That class vanishes if and only if the reduction admits a global torsion-free compatible connection. When it vanishes, all such connections form an affine space modelled on smooth sections of the associated bundle with fibre \(\mathfrak h^{(1)}\).

**Proposition 10.2 (orthogonal case).** If \(g\) is a nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form and \(\mathfrak h=\mathfrak{so}(V,g)\), the map \(\delta\) in (10.1) is an isomorphism. Every smooth nondegenerate metric therefore has exactly one torsion-free metric-compatible connection, in any signature.

Smoothly generated immersed subgroup, countable topology and regularity; finite lasso factorization and countable fundamental group; full/restricted holonomy including original piecewise C1 path generality.
All worked examples and four complete exercises, including dense nonclosed flat torus holonomy.
All graded derivations and insertion; FN and insertion brackets; projection curvature/cocurvature identities; arbitrary-map naturality; general Ehresmann Bianchi; three complete exercises.

Intrinsic torsion and global compatible extension; pseudo-orthogonal and symplectic cases; both Berger criteria; all real irreducible sl2 modules; all-degree binary curvature restrictions and cubic prolongations; quartic parallel curvature; all exercises.

Admissible Poisson maps, regular local symplectic realization, torsion-free realization and actual analytic nonparallel cubic holonomy; complete cubic equations, analytic germ determination and real/complex tests; all exercises.
Spencer complex and contraction; complete GL tensor-product curvature spaces; orthogonal/symplectic restrictions and parallelness; product first-jet sequence and exercises.

Real and complex infinite exotic holonomy families, all signatures/dimensions; invariant normalization, injective curvature map, full-span tensor, actual nonlinear analytic existence; realification/kernel/invariant-form exercises.

Full hypotheses and structure equations; analyticity and germ determination; complete bilinear compatibility spaces including realification; entire curvature and derivative spaces, ordinary prolongation and full infinite-family consequences; all exercises.

Smooth/analytic symplectic realization at every Poisson point, including rank change; spray/endpoint signs, arbitrary-spray extension, worked rank-changing example; full structure-equation converse at singular data and dimension exercise.
